why: The density fixture, and the first one in this set that reproduces the miss. Every other ticket here is written clean enough that the finding it exists for is the only thing in it, and what would settle the open questions those fixtures leave behind is a fixture at a real card's density instead. This is that: 4,671 characters of description against ORC-107's 1,254, seven sections, a background, seven acceptance criteria, a section of things explicitly already decided, and an out-of-scope list. One outcome, one surface, the role, the resets, what counts and what does not, the API half, the patient app, the number itself and whether it is configurable - the card answers all of them, at length, which is the point. What is not settled has to compete with a screenful of what is. It also carries more than one unsettled thing, deliberately, because a real card does. Measured over four fresh single-round samples under the shipped code: the first read returned ready on three of the four, and on all three the adversarial re-read found a blocking product question and the round became needs_input; on the fourth the first read found one itself. All four rounds converged on the same question - whether requests a clinic already made earlier in the month count against its three when the cap goes live - which one read finds in 1 of 4 samples and the pass finds in 4 of 4. That is the whole argument for the pass, in one card. Read two things carefully before trusting this fixture further. It is set on the verdict rather than on a particular question: which ambiguity gets named varies, and the one the card was written around - whether the three belong to each doctor or to the clinic between them - was named in only one of the four samples, because both reads mostly resolve it to the clinic without noticing they had a choice. And the budget of three is one above the highest total any of the four rounds asked (0, 1, 1 and 2), so it is there to catch a second read that pads rather than to pin the count; only the verdict is the gate.
